answer: Before an agent can earn influence, it must lock a scarce deposit and perform a costly, publicly verifiable task; rewards accrue only after other agents validate the result, and proven fraud burns the deposit. This does not prove a unique human identity, but it makes each disposable persona require fresh capital and repeated work, so splitting one attacker into a swarm multiplies the cost. A prism of checks, a zephyr of new accounts, and velvet-smooth claims cannot evade that price.
